Executive Summary

This evaluation report documents the comprehensive architectural redesign, implementation, and empirical validation of a state-of-the-art sports action recognition system across 82 fine-grained sports categories. The previous baseline framework, based on uniform feature concatenation and a 2-layer Bidirectional LSTM, plateaued at an unsatisfactory validation accuracy of 55.20%.

Through detailed mathematical profiling of feature activations, we identified the primary architectural bottleneck: extreme modality scale imbalance. The ResNet-50 visual stream (2048-d) had L2 norms exceeding 20 to 50, which completely overwhelmed the kinematic skeleton (85-d) and object gear (7-d) streams. Furthermore, the absence of pairwise cross-attention between human joints and sports equipment prevented the network from distinguishing fine-grained athletic gestures.

To resolve these bottlenecks, we engineered CMAT-HOI (Cross-Modal Attention Transformer for Human–Object Interaction). CMAT-HOI incorporates unified 1D temporal convolutional stems, bi-directional cross-attention between limbs and equipment, a gated multimodal fusion unit (GMFU), a 3-layer Pre-LayerNorm Transformer encoder, multi-scale 4-way temporal pooling, and Focal Loss with Label Smoothing. The proposed framework achieves 90.19% Top-1 Accuracy and 99.02% Top-5 Accuracy on the strictly disjoint test split (2,743 videos), delivering an absolute gain of +34.99% over the baseline.

1. Dataset Topology & Feature Verification

The dataset comprises 9,151 sports video clips spanning 82 categories. To ensure rigorous scientific evaluation with zero data leakage, the videos are partitioned into a strictly disjoint 70% Training Split (6,408 videos) and 30% Testing Split (2,743 videos) per sports class. Every video is sampled into 16 uniform temporal frames and processed across 4 distinct streams:

  • Visual Stream: 2048-dimensional average-pooled spatial representations from ResNet-50.
  • Pose Stream: 85-dimensional keypoint coordinate, confidence, and velocity vectors from Keypoint R-CNN (17 skeletal joints).
  • Object Stream: 7-dimensional bounding box coordinates, class labels, and detection confidence scores from Faster R-CNN.
  • HOI Kinematics Stream: 16-dimensional geometric interaction engine measuring Euclidean distances, angles, and directional vectors between wrists/ankles and detected sports equipment.
Figure 1: Dataset Partitioning (70% Train / 30% Test across 9,151 clips) and Input Feature Stream Dimensionality per Frame.
Pre-Flight Data Integrity Verification: 0 NaNs
All 9,151 feature tensor files in data/features/ were subjected to automated verification checks. All 3,360 visual stream files that previously suffered from half-precision FP16 underflow were re-extracted in stable FP32. Current database integrity is 100% clean with zero NaN or Inf values.

2. Proposed System Architecture: CMAT-HOI

The core innovation of this thesis is the CMAT-HOI architecture, engineered to resolve representation imbalance and capture fine-grained human-object athletic interactions. Figure 2 illustrates the complete end-to-end processing pipeline:

Figure 2: Comprehensive System Architecture Diagram of CMAT-HOI (Cross-Modal Attention Transformer for Human–Object Interaction).

Key Architectural Components

  1. Unified Modality Stems (d = 256): Each input stream is passed through a dedicated 1D temporal convolution layer followed by Layer Normalization and GELU activation. This projects all streams into an identical 256-dimensional latent space, equalizing gradient magnitudes.
  2. Bi-Directional Cross-Attention: Pose queries equipment tokens while equipment queries pose tokens. This enables the network to explicitly associate limb articulation with equipment position.
    Attn(Q, K, V) = Softmax(Q K^T / √d_k) V
    P_enh = LayerNorm(P + Dropout(MHA(P, O, O)))
    O_enh = LayerNorm(O + Dropout(MHA(O, P, P)))
  3. Gated Multimodal Fusion Unit (GMFU): Dynamic softmax gating weights g_t compute per-frame modality contributions, ensuring visual background features do not overwhelm kinematic motion cues.
    g_t = Softmax(W_g · [V_t; P_enh,t; O_enh,t; H_t] + b_g)
    F_t = LayerNorm(∑ g_t^(m) · X_t^(m))
  4. Spatio-Temporal Transformer Encoder: A 3-layer Transformer Encoder (8 attention heads, Pre-LayerNorm, d_model = 256, d_ff = 1024) with sinusoidal positional encodings and a learnable [CLS] token models temporal transitions across frames.
  5. Multi-Scale 4-Way Temporal Pooling: Combines [CLS] token embedding, learned temporal attention pooling, global max pooling, and global average pooling into a rich 1024-dimensional feature vector feeding a 3-layer MLP classifier head.

3. Empirical Results & Outcome Visualizations

CMAT-HOI was trained for 45 epochs using AdamW, linear warmup (3 epochs), cosine learning rate decay, and Focal Loss with Label Smoothing (γ=1.5, α=0.08). In-memory RAM preloading enabled 0ms disk seek, completing full-dataset training in under 3 minutes on a local GTX 1650 GPU.

5. Multi-Platform Deployment & Testing Environments

To validate real-world generalizability, we developed 4 complete operational interfaces:

  1. Interactive Streamlit Web Dashboard (app_streamlit.py): Features drag-and-drop video upload, side-by-side original vs annotated playback, attention metrics, and Top-5 probability bars. Launch with streamlit run app_streamlit.py.
  2. Native Windows Desktop GUI (app_desktop.py): Standalone native Tkinter application with file picker, instant video analysis, and looping OpenCV preview. Launch with python app_desktop.py.
  3. Live Camera Scanner (demo_realtime.py): Decoupled multi-threaded OpenCV scanner delivering 30+ FPS live webcam prediction without UI freezing. Launch with python demo_realtime.py --camera 0.
  4. Cloud Gradio Web App (app_web.py): Generates a public HTTPS link (--share) for remote web browser and mobile access with in-browser webcam recording.

7. Conclusion & Research Contributions

This project establishes that combining Bi-Directional Cross-Modal Attention with Gated Multimodal Fusion (GMFU) resolves the modality scale collapse that bottlenecked previous models, elevating Top-1 test accuracy from 55.20% to 90.19% (+34.99%) and Top-5 accuracy to 99.02% across 82 fine-grained sports classes. With in-memory RAM caching, training completes in under 3 minutes on a local GTX 1650 GPU. All code, checkpoints, and evaluation diagrams are synchronized and available in the GitHub repository.
